KO.rationale: Coca-Cola's franchise quality is elite — asset-light model, ~46% global sparkling share, 64-year dividend streak, 40.4% ROE, 25.9% net margin, and Q1 2026 revenue beat of 11-12% YoY confirming ongoing pricing power and portfolio momentum. However, the stock is priced at the ceiling of its own valuation range: trailing PE of 28.7x (vs 23.2-29.0x 365d range), P/B at 11.6x (vs 9.4-11.7x range), and earnings yield of 3.5% sitting below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.57% — a negative equity risk premium. Oil at $100/bbl (+51% over 90 days) creates input-cost headwinds for packaging and transport. The Q1 2026 earnings beat is a modest positive catalyst but is already reflected in the stock's ~24% rally off its $65.35 low, with price now consolidating near $81.17 highs and fading momentum (Q1 2026 only +1.7%). Forward PE of ~24x (Yahoo Finance) is more reasonable than the 28.7x trailing, but still commands a significant premium to PepsiCo's ~17x. Net: excellent business, fully priced at the top of its historical range with limited margin of safety in a rising-rate, rising-oil environment. The score reflects strong fundamentals offset by stretched valuation, yielding a mildly positive but constrained rating.
